-- CLAUDE.md --
# mygame

A 2D game on the Weakpixel Engine (`github.com/weakpixel/engine`, an ECS plus a runtime on Ebiten). README.md lists the files and commands.

## Where things are

- `game/`: the game. Components and Game Objects (`+game:*` markers) in `components.go`, one system per file, settings and actions in `game.go`.
- `main.go`: window only. `editor.go`: the VSCode editor build (`-tags editor`).
- `assets/`: the asset library. Asset keys are paths from `assets/`. Levels are `*.level.json`, prefabs `*.prefab.json`.

## Rules

- Never edit generated files by hand: `game/zz__gen.go` and `build/god/*.god.json`. Change the markers and run `go generate ./...`; commit `game/zz__gen.go` (the GOD files in `build/god/` are build output and stay out of git).
- Systems read input actions (`game.go`, bound in `assets/global/input/player.bindings.json`), never keys.
- Run `go test ./...` after a change, and `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build .` when it touches the browser build.

## Engine docs

The engine's documentation is the spec: https://github.com/weakpixel/engine/tree/main/doc/guide. Start with `engine/getting-started.md`, `ecs/api-game-object.md`, `engine/asset-library.md`, `engine/input.md` and `engine/editor.md`.
-- Makefile --
# The game's everyday commands. Every tool runs through "go tool wpix",
# at the engine version in go.mod.

GOROOT := $(shell go env GOROOT)

.PHONY: run dev generate test check doc web web-packed web-dev editor serve clean

# The game in a window, with the embedded assets.
run:
	go run .

# The game reading assets/ from disk: saved changes reload while it runs.
dev:
	go run . -assets assets

# Game Object code (game/zz__gen.go) and GOD files (build/god/, not committed) from the +game markers,
# and the embed list of the assets (zz__gen.assets_embed.go, without what assets/.assetignore ignores).
generate:
	go generate ./...

# The game's tests, and the editor build's (editor_test.go).
test:
	go test ./...
	go test -tags editor .

# Checks the asset library: file names, groups, broken references.
check:
	go tool wpix assets check

# The merged GOD (build/god/project.god.json) and HTML docs of every Game Object (build/god-doc).
doc:
	go tool wpix doc --format god
	go tool wpix doc

# The browser build in build/web, assets embedded. Serve it with make serve.
web:
	mkdir -p build/web
	GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build -o build/web/game.wasm .
	cp "$(GOROOT)/lib/wasm/wasm_exec.js" web/index.html build/web/

# The browser build in build/web-packed: the assets as packs, fetched over HTTP.
web-packed:
	rm -rf build/web-packed
	mkdir -p build/web-packed
	GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build -tags webassets -o build/web-packed/game.wasm .
	cp "$(GOROOT)/lib/wasm/wasm_exec.js" web/index.html build/web-packed/
	go run . -pack build/web-packed/assets

# The browser build for development, at http://localhost:8080: it reads the loose
# files of assets/ from a dev server that pushes changes, so a file you save
# (a shader, a texture, a map) reloads in the open page without a refresh.
web-dev:
	rm -rf build/web-dev
	mkdir -p build/web-dev
	GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build -tags webassets,webdev -o build/web-dev/game.wasm .
	cp "$(GOROOT)/lib/wasm/wasm_exec.js" web/index.html build/web-dev/
	go tool wpix serve --assets assets build/web-dev

# The level editor in a window, without VSCode.
editor:
	go run -tags editor .

# Serves build/web on http://localhost:8080 (any static file server works).
serve:
	python3 -m http.server 8080 -d build/web

clean:
	rm -rf build
-- README.md --
# mygame

A game on the [Weakpixel Engine](https://github.com/weakpixel/engine), created with `wpix new`.

```sh
make run      # play: WASD or the arrow keys walk, Shift runs, Esc quits
make test     # the game's tests, without a window
```

## Commands

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `make run` | The game in a window, with the assets embedded in the binary |
| `make dev` | The game reading `assets/` from disk: files you save reload while it runs |
| `make generate` | `go generate ./...`: Game Object code (`game/zz__gen.go`) and the GOD file (`build/god/mygame.god.json`) from the `+game` markers. Run it after changing a component |
| `make test` | `go test ./...`, then the editor build's test (`go test -tags editor .`) |
| `make check` | Checks the asset library: file names, groups and broken references |
| `make doc` | The merged GOD (`build/god/project.god.json`) and HTML docs of the Game Objects (`build/god-doc/`) |
| `make web` | The browser build in `build/web/`; `make serve` serves it on http://localhost:8080 |
| `make web-packed` | The browser build with the assets as packs, fetched over HTTP, in `build/web-packed/` |
| `make web-dev` | The browser build for development: serves it on http://localhost:8080 and reloads the assets you save in the open page |
| `make editor` | The level editor in a window, without VSCode |

The engine's command-line tools run as `go tool wpix <command>` at the engine version in `go.mod` (`go tool wpix help` lists them). `go tool wpix-editor assets/<file>.png` opens a texture in the engine's preview, with a grid, pan and zoom; any asset file opens in the tool of its kind (`go tool wpix-editor help` lists them).

## Files

| Path | What |
| --- | --- |
| `main.go` | Opens the window and runs the game; `-assets <dir>` reads loose files, `-pack <dir>` writes the packed build |
| `assets.go`, `assets_web.go` | Where the assets come from: embedded, or packs over HTTP in the `webassets` browser build |
| `zz__gen.assets_embed.go` | The embed list of `assets/`, written by `make generate` |
| `watch.go`, `watch_web.go` | Pushed asset changes for hot reload: none, or from the dev server in the `webdev` browser build |
| `editor.go` | The editor build (`-tags editor`) that the VSCode extension runs |
| `main_test.go`, `editor_test.go` | Run the game, and the editor build, without a window: the player walks, the editor opens the level |
| `game/game.go` | Settings, input actions, `AddSystems` and the first level |
| `game/components.go` | The `PlayerControl` component and the `Player` Game Object |
| `game/player-system.go` | Moves the player by the move action |
| `assets/` | The [asset library](https://github.com/weakpixel/engine/blob/main/doc/guide/engine/asset-library.md#the-layout): `global/` loads at start, every other folder is a package (`start/` holds the first level) |
| `assets/.assetignore` | Files in `assets/` the game does not ship ([`.gitignore` syntax](https://github.com/weakpixel/engine/blob/main/doc/guide/engine/asset-library.md#ignoring-files)) |
| `assets/start/start.level.json` | The first level. Open it in VSCode to edit it |
| `assets/global/prefabs/player.prefab.json` | The player prefab the level places |
| `assets/global/input/player.bindings.json` | Keys and gamepad buttons of the actions |
| `build/god/` | Generated GOD files (not committed): the schema of every Game Object, read by the editor extension. Run `go generate ./...` once after cloning |
| `web/index.html` | The page of the browser build |
| `.weakpixel.json` | [Project settings](https://github.com/weakpixel/engine/blob/main/doc/guide/project-file.md) for the tools and the editor |

## Editing levels in VSCode

Install the [Weakpixel VSCode extension](https://github.com/weakpixel/weakpixel-engine-vscode) (`.vscode/extensions.json` recommends it) and open `assets/start/start.level.json`: the game runs in the editor tab, and every change is written into the file.

## Learn more

- [Getting started](https://github.com/weakpixel/engine/blob/main/doc/guide/engine/getting-started.md) and the [engine guide](https://github.com/weakpixel/engine/blob/main/doc/guide/engine/README.md)
- [Game Objects and markers](https://github.com/weakpixel/engine/blob/main/doc/guide/ecs/api-game-object.md)
- [Input actions](https://github.com/weakpixel/engine/blob/main/doc/guide/engine/input.md)
- [Tools](https://github.com/weakpixel/engine/blob/main/doc/guide/tools.md)
-- assets.go --
//go:build !editor && !(js && webassets)

package main

import "io/fs"

// assets is the game's asset library (doc/guide/engine/asset-library.md),
// embedded in the binary so that it runs anywhere, the browser included. The
// variable is in zz__gen.assets_embed.go: wpix assets embed writes its
// go:embed patterns so that the files assets/.assetignore ignores stay out
// (make generate after changing an .assetignore).
//
//go:generate go tool wpix assets embed assets --tags "!editor && !(js && webassets)" -o zz__gen.assets_embed.go

// gameAssets is the library the game runs on: the embedded assets folder.
func gameAssets() (fs.FS, error) { return fs.Sub(assets, "assets") }
-- assets/.assetignore --
# Files in assets/ that the game does not ship: they are not embedded,
# packed or loaded. The syntax is that of .gitignore, and an .assetignore
# in a folder applies to the files below it. go tool wpix assets ls --ignored
# lists what is ignored; run make generate after a change.
#
# *.aseprite
# *.psd
# drafts/

-- assets_test.go --
//go:build !editor && !(js && webassets)

package main

import (
	"os"
	"testing"

	"github.com/weakpixel/engine/asset/library"
)

// TestEmbeddedAssetsMatchLibrary fails when zz__gen.assets_embed.go is
// stale: a file was added where the embed list names single files, or an
// .assetignore changed. Run make generate.
func TestEmbeddedAssetsMatchLibrary(t *testing.T) {
	embedded, err := gameAssets()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	missing, extra, err := library.DiffFiles(os.DirFS("assets"), embedded)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(missing) > 0 || len(extra) > 0 {
		t.Fatalf("the embedded assets differ from assets/ (run make generate):\nnot embedded: %v\nembedded but ignored: %v", missing, extra)
	}
}
-- assets_web.go --
//go:build !editor && js && webassets

package main

import (
	"io/fs"
	"syscall/js"

	"github.com/weakpixel/asset/httpfs"
)

// gameAssets is the library a browser build with the webassets tag runs on:
// the packed build (go run . -pack) served in assets/ next to the page and
// read over HTTP, one pack per group as the game loads it. The game embeds
// nothing, so the download starts sooner (make web-packed).
func gameAssets() (fs.FS, error) {
	href := js.Global().Get("location").Get("href").String()
	base := js.Global().Get("URL").New("assets/", href).Get("href").String()
	return httpfs.New(base, nil)
}
-- editor.go --
//go:build editor

package main

import (
	"io/fs"
	"log"
	"os"

	"github.com/weakpixel/engine/editor/host"
	engine "github.com/weakpixel/engine/game"

	"example.com/mygame/game"
)

// main is the editor build's entry: the VSCode extension builds this
// package with -tags editor to WebAssembly and shows the game in the level
// editor (go run -tags editor . opens the editor in a window). The host
// connects the editor and opens the level; the game only adds its systems.
// See doc/guide/engine/editor.md#making-a-game-editable-in-vscode.
func main() {
	if err := host.Run(editorGame()); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}

// editorGame describes the game to the editor host.
func editorGame() host.Game {
	return host.Game{
		FS:    diskAssets,
		Level: game.FirstLevel,
		Config: func(fsys fs.FS) (engine.Config, error) {
			return game.Config(engine.Config{}, fsys)
		},
		Setup: game.AddSystems,
	}
}

// diskAssets is the assets folder on disk: the editor build embeds nothing.
// In VSCode the workspace's files are read over HTTP instead and there is no
// folder.
func diskAssets() (fs.FS, error) {
	if st, err := os.Stat("assets"); err == nil && st.IsDir() {
		return os.DirFS("assets"), nil
	}
	return nil, nil
}
-- editor_test.go --
//go:build editor

package main

import (
	"io/fs"
	"slices"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/weakpixel/engine/editor/host"
	engine "github.com/weakpixel/engine/game"
)

// TestEditorBuild builds the editor build without a window (go test -tags
// editor .): the game starts paused on the first level, whose objects belong
// to the editor session.
func TestEditorBuild(t *testing.T) {
	g := editorGame()
	config := g.Config
	g.Config = func(fsys fs.FS) (engine.Config, error) {
		cfg, err := config(fsys)
		cfg.NoAudio = true
		return cfg, err
	}
	e, s, err := host.Build(g, host.Page{}) // no VSCode page outside a browser
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer e.Close()
	// The level spawns once its prefab has loaded on a worker goroutine:
	// wait in real time, not in ticks.
	deadline := time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second)
	for !slices.Contains(s.IDs(), "player") {
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			t.Fatalf("editor objects %v, want the player", s.IDs())
		}
		if err := e.Update(); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		time.Sleep(time.Millisecond)
	}
	if !e.Paused() {
		t.Error("the editor build does not start paused")
	}
}
-- game/components.go --
package game

import "github.com/weakpixel/engine/gfx"

// Components are plain structs. A +game:component marker makes one a Game
// Object component: levels and prefabs can set it, and the editor's
// inspector shows its fields. A +game:object groups components into a class
// with a typed view (zz__gen.go). See doc/guide/ecs/api-game-object.md.

// PlayerControl makes an entity walk where the player steers it.
// +game:component
type PlayerControl struct {
	// Speed is the walking speed in world units per second.
	Speed float32
	// RunSpeed is the speed while the run action is held.
	RunSpeed float32
}

// Player is the character the player steers: a sprite that walks.
// global/prefabs/player.prefab.json is one, and the first level places it.
// +game:object
type Player struct {
	// Where the player is and how it looks.
	// +game:embed
	gfx.Visual
	// How fast it walks.
	// +game:component
	Control *PlayerControl
}
-- game/game.go --
// +game:group:name=mygame
//
// Package game is the game: its components and Game Objects, its systems and
// its input actions. The main package only opens a window around it, and the
// editor build (editor.go) runs the same systems inside the VSCode level
// editor.
package game

import (
	"image/color"
	"io/fs"
	"log"

	"github.com/weakpixel/ecs/system"
	"github.com/weakpixel/engine/asset/library"
	engine "github.com/weakpixel/engine/game"
	"github.com/weakpixel/engine/input"
	"github.com/weakpixel/engine/render"
)

// go generate writes zz__gen.go (the typed views of the Game Objects in
// components.go) and the GOD file god/mygame.god.json, which the level
// editor reads.
//go:generate go tool wpix gen

// Asset keys: paths from the library root, assets/.
const (
	// FirstLevel is the level the game starts in and the editor opens. It
	// lives in the library package start/.
	FirstLevel = "start/start.level.json"
	// bindings binds the actions below to keys and gamepad buttons.
	bindings = "global/input/player.bindings.json"
)

// gameplay is the mapping of the bindings file that holds the bindings of
// the actions while the game is played (a menu would get its own).
const gameplay = "gameplay"

// Actions is what the player can do, declared in Go and bound to devices in
// the bindings file. Systems read action state, never keys
// (doc/guide/engine/input.md).
type Actions struct {
	*input.Actions
	Move input.Action // Vec2: walking direction
	Run  input.Action // Button: hold to run
	Quit input.Action // Button: leave the game
}

// actions is the game's action table. It is frozen, so every engine can
// share it.
var actions = newActions()

func newActions() *Actions {
	a := &Actions{Actions: &input.Actions{}}
	a.Move = a.Vec2("move", "Walk.")
	a.Run = a.Button("run", "Hold to run.")
	a.Quit = a.Button("quit", "Leave the game.")
	a.Freeze()
	return a
}

// Config adds the game's settings to cfg: the asset library at the root of
// fsys, the resolution, the camera and the input actions.
func Config(cfg engine.Config, fsys fs.FS) (engine.Config, error) {
	lib, err := library.Open(fsys)
	if err != nil {
		return cfg, err
	}
	cfg.Library = lib
	cfg.Width, cfg.Height = 320, 180
	cfg.Background = color.RGBA{R: 20, G: 18, B: 26, A: 255}
	cfg.Camera = render.Camera{Zoom: 1}
	cfg.Input.Actions = actions.Actions
	cfg.Input.Bindings = bindings
	// Development hotkey: F12 saves the frame as a PNG in screenshots/ (F9
	// in a browser, which keeps F12 for its developer tools). Under the
	// editor the PNG goes to VSCode. Delete the line to turn it off.
	cfg.Screenshots.Key = engine.DevScreenshotKey()
	return cfg, nil
}

// AddSystems adds the game's systems to e. The editor build calls it too:
// there the systems run when you press Play.
func AddSystems(e *engine.Engine) {
	e.AddRunner(engine.StageSimulate, &PlayerSystem{})
}

// LoadFirstLevel loads FirstLevel. The editor build does not call it: the
// editor opens the level itself.
func LoadFirstLevel(e *engine.Engine) {
	e.AddRunner(engine.StageSimulate, levelLoader{})
}

// levelLoader loads FirstLevel before the first tick: at once from loose or
// embedded files, a few ticks later from a pack (the webassets build), once
// the pack of its package is mounted. It is a system.Runner.
type levelLoader struct{}

// Init starts loading the level.
func (levelLoader) Init(ctx *system.Context) {
	if _, err := engine.EngineOf(ctx).LoadLevel(FirstLevel); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}

// Run does nothing: the engine spawns the level.
func (levelLoader) Run(*system.Context) {}
-- game/player-system.go --
package game

import (
	"github.com/weakpixel/ecs/system"
	engine "github.com/weakpixel/engine/game"
)

// PlayerSystem walks every Player in the direction of the move action, and
// quits the game on the quit action. It is a system.Runner: Init runs once
// before the first tick, Run every tick.
type PlayerSystem struct {
	e       *engine.Engine
	players PlayerView
}

// Init creates the typed view of the Player objects (generated in
// zz__gen.go; create views once, not every tick) and turns on the bindings
// of the gameplay mapping for player 0.
func (s *PlayerSystem) Init(ctx *system.Context) {
	s.e = engine.EngineOf(ctx)
	s.players = NewPlayerView(ctx.World)
	s.e.Input().Player(0).Push(gameplay)
}

// Run moves the players by this tick's input.
func (s *PlayerSystem) Run(ctx *system.Context) {
	st := s.e.Input().Player(0).State()
	if st.JustPressed(actions.Quit) {
		s.e.Quit()
	}
	x, y := st.Vec2(actions.Move)
	dt := float32(ctx.Time.Delta.Seconds())
	for _, p := range s.players.Each() {
		speed := p.Control.Speed
		if st.Down(actions.Run) {
			speed = p.Control.RunSpeed
		}
		p.Transform.Pos.X += x * speed * dt
		p.Transform.Pos.Y += y * speed * dt
	}
}
-- go.mod --
module example.com/mygame

go 1.27

require (
	github.com/weakpixel/asset v0.0.1
	github.com/weakpixel/ecs v0.0.1
	github.com/weakpixel/engine v0.1.2
)

tool (
	github.com/weakpixel/engine/tools/wpix-editor
	github.com/weakpixel/engine/tools/wpix
)
-- main.go --
//go:build !editor

// Command mygame runs the game in a window:
//
//	go run .                  the assets embedded in the binary
//	go run . -assets assets   the assets folder, reloading files you change
//	go run . -pack <dir>      write the packed build of the assets and exit
//
// The game itself is in package game; this file only opens the window.
package main

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"log"
	"os"
	"time"

	"github.com/hajimehoshi/ebiten/v2"

	"github.com/weakpixel/engine/asset/library"
	engine "github.com/weakpixel/engine/game"

	"example.com/mygame/game"
)

func main() {
	dir := flag.String("assets", "", "read the assets from this folder instead of the embedded ones, and reload changed files")
	pack := flag.String("pack", "", "write the packed build of the assets to this empty directory and exit")
	flag.Parse()

	var cfg engine.Config
	// The startup screen shows while the first assets load, for at least 5
	// seconds. Replace or add screens in StartupConfig; delete this line to
	// start the game at once. Tests and the editor build leave it off.
	cfg.Startup = &engine.StartupConfig{}
	cfg.AssetChanges = assetChanges()
	fsys, err := gameAssets()
	if *dir != "" {
		fsys, err = os.DirFS(*dir), nil
		cfg.WatchInterval = time.Second / 2
	}
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	if *pack != "" {
		packAssets(fsys, *pack)
		return
	}

	e, err := newGame(cfg, fsys)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	ebiten.SetWindowSize(1280, 720)
	ebiten.SetWindowTitle("mygame")
	ebiten.SetWindowResizingMode(ebiten.WindowResizingModeEnabled)
	runErr := ebiten.RunGame(e)
	e.Close()
	if runErr != nil {
		log.Fatal(runErr)
	}
}

// newGame builds the engine on the asset library at the root of fsys and
// starts the first level. main runs it in a window; main_test.go ticks it
// without one. cfg adds to the game's own settings (the test sets its input
// source).
func newGame(cfg engine.Config, fsys fs.FS) (*engine.Engine, error) {
	cfg, err := game.Config(cfg, fsys)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	e := engine.New(cfg)
	game.AddSystems(e)
	game.LoadFirstLevel(e)
	return e, nil
}

// packAssets writes the packed build of fsys to dir: one pack per group and
// a catalog, which the browser build with the webassets tag reads over HTTP
// (make web-packed).
func packAssets(fsys fs.FS, dir string) {
	cat, _, err := library.WritePacks(fsys, dir)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, g := range cat.Packages {
		fmt.Printf("%s -> %s\n", g.Name, g.Pack)
	}
}
-- main_test.go --
//go:build !editor

package main

import (
	"testing"
	"time"

	engine "github.com/weakpixel/engine/game"
	"github.com/weakpixel/engine/gfx"
	"github.com/weakpixel/engine/input"

	"example.com/mygame/game"
)

// TestPlayerWalks runs the game without a window: it waits until the first
// level has spawned the player, then holds D for half a second and checks
// that the player walked right. Copy it for your own systems.
func TestPlayerWalks(t *testing.T) {
	src := &input.ManualSource{}
	src.Frame.Width, src.Frame.Height = 320, 180
	fsys, err := gameAssets()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	e, err := newGame(engine.Config{NoAudio: true, Input: engine.InputConfig{Source: src}}, fsys)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer e.Close()
	players := game.NewPlayerView(e.World())

	// Assets load on worker goroutines: wait in real time, not in ticks.
	deadline := time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second)
	start, ok := playerPos(players)
	for !ok {
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			t.Fatal("the first level never spawned a player")
		}
		if err := e.Update(); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		time.Sleep(time.Millisecond)
		start, ok = playerPos(players)
	}

	src.Frame.Keys.Set(input.KeyD)
	for range 30 {
		if err := e.Update(); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	if got, _ := playerPos(players); got.X <= start.X || got.Y != start.Y {
		t.Errorf("the player moved from %v to %v, want to the right", start, got)
	}
}

// playerPos is the position of the first player; ok is false while there
// is none.
func playerPos(players game.PlayerView) (pos gfx.Vec2, ok bool) {
	for _, p := range players.Each() {
		return p.Transform.Pos, true
	}
	return gfx.Vec2{}, false
}

//go:build !editor && !(js && webassets && webdev)

package main

// assetChanges is the source of pushed asset changes (game.Config.AssetChanges):
// none here. The browser dev build (make web-dev) has one, see watch_web.go.
func assetChanges() <-chan []string { return nil }
-- watch_web.go --
//go:build !editor && js && webassets && webdev

package main

import (
	"syscall/js"

	"github.com/weakpixel/asset/httpfs"
)

// assetChanges listens to the dev server (go tool wpix serve), which
// sends the keys of the asset files you save, so the open page reloads them
// without a refresh (make web-dev).
func assetChanges() <-chan []string {
	href := js.Global().Get("location").Get("href").String()
	url := js.Global().Get("URL").New("_weakpixel/changes", href).Get("href").String()
	return httpfs.WatchChanges(url)
}
-- web/index.html --
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>mygame</title>
<!--
  Web shell for an game build (doc/guide/engine/web.md). build.sh puts
  this file next to game.wasm and Go's wasm_exec.js. Ebiten adds its own
  canvas to <body> and scales it to the window.
-->
<style>
  html, body { margin: 0; height: 100%; background: #141218; color: #ddd; font: 14px system-ui, sans-serif; }
  #overlay { position: fixed; inset: 0; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
             background: rgba(20, 18, 24, 0.85); cursor: pointer; z-index: 10; text-align: center; }
  #overlay.hidden { display: none; }
  #error { position: fixed; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; max-height: 50%; overflow: auto; margin: 0;
           padding: 8px 12px; background: #3a0d12; color: #ffd7d7; white-space: pre-wrap; z-index: 20; }
  #error:empty { display: none; }
</style>
</head>
<body>
<div id="overlay"><div id="status">Loading…</div></div>
<pre id="error"></pre>
<script src="wasm_exec.js"></script>
<script>
"use strict";
const overlay = document.getElementById("overlay");
const statusText = document.getElementById("status");
const errorBox = document.getElementById("error");

// Go writes panics and log output through console.log/console.error (see
// wasm_exec.js). Once a panic starts, every following line goes to the
// error box too, so the stack trace is readable on the page.
let failing = false;
for (const name of ["log", "error"]) {
  const orig = console[name].bind(console);
  console[name] = (...args) => {
    const line = args.join(" ");
    if (/^(panic: |fatal error: |exit code: [1-9])/.test(line)) failing = true;
    if (failing) errorBox.textContent += line + "\n";
    orig(...args);
  };
}

// The first click (or key) starts the game. It focuses the page and counts
// as the user gesture browsers require before audio may play (Ebiten resumes
// its AudioContext on the first input it sees). Starting the game only then
// means its startup screen and minimum time run in view, not behind this
// overlay (doc/guide/engine/engine.md#startup-screen).
const clicked = new Promise((resolve) => {
  const start = () => {
    overlay.classList.add("hidden");
    window.focus();
    resolve();
  };
  overlay.addEventListener("click", start, { once: true });
  window.addEventListener("keydown", start, { once: true });
});

// fetchWithProgress downloads the module and shows how much has arrived.
async function fetchWithProgress(url) {
  const resp = await fetch(url);
  if (!resp.ok) throw new Error(`${url}: HTTP ${resp.status}`);
  const total = Number(resp.headers.get("Content-Length")) || 0;
  const reader = resp.body.getReader();
  const chunks = [];
  let got = 0;
  for (;;) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    chunks.push(value);
    got += value.length;
    statusText.textContent = total
      ? `Loading… ${Math.round(got / total * 100)}%`
      : `Loading… ${(got / 1048576).toFixed(1)} MB`;
  }
  return new Blob(chunks).arrayBuffer();
}

(async () => {
  try {
    const go = new Go();
    const bytes = await fetchWithProgress("game.wasm");
    const { instance } = await WebAssembly.instantiate(bytes, go.importObject);
    statusText.textContent = "Click to start";
    await clicked;
    // go.run creates Ebiten's canvas before it first yields.
    const run = go.run(instance);
    const canvas = document.querySelector("canvas");
    if (canvas) canvas.focus();
    await run;
    if (!failing) statusText.textContent = "The game has ended.";
    overlay.classList.remove("hidden");
  } catch (err) {
    errorBox.textContent += String(err && err.stack || err) + "\n";
  }
})();
</script>
</body>
</html>
